language_wrapper: In base {base}, consider all {length}-digit integers whose digits are drawn (allowing repetition) from the allowed set [{allowed_digits_csv}]. A number is valid if it is divisible by each of its digits, divisible by the sum of its digits, and divisible by {length}. Determine the sum, in base 10, of all valid numbers.
hardness_rationale: The seed asks for two-digit base-10 numbers divisible by each digit, which reduces to simple divisibility and a small case check. Our family generalizes to base b in {9,10,11,12}, length 3 or 4, allows a parameterized digit set, and imposes three simultaneous divisibility constraints: by each digit, by the sum of digits, and by the length. This creates a coupled system of congruences N ≡ 0 mod d for every digit d and N ≡ 0 mod sum(digits), together with base-dependent interactions N = sum d_i b^{position}. Solving such instances demands deeper modular reasoning (e.g., analyzing N modulo each digit and modulo the digit sum using the base’s residues), and careful structural pruning, far beyond the straightforward two-digit case. The verifier enforces a minimum number of solutions to avoid trivial edge cases, ensuring a genuinely challenging enumeration and reasoning task.
notes: Correctness proof sketch for the family: Let N be an L-digit number in base b with digits d_1,...,d_L from the allowed set (nonzero). The conditions are (i) d_j | N for every j, (ii) s := d_1+...+d_L divides N, and (iii) L divides N. Since N = sum_{i=1}^L d_i b^{L-i}, the condition d_j | N is equivalent to d_j | sum_{i != j} d_i b^{L-i} because d_j clearly divides the jth term d_j b^{L-j}; thus each digit imposes a nontrivial modular constraint involving powers of b modulo d_j. Condition (ii) imposes N ≡ 0 (mod s), which again is a modular condition depending on b’s powers modulo s. Condition (iii) is independent and requires N ≡ 0 (mod L). Therefore, any valid N must be a simultaneous solution to these congruences. The verifier computes N explicitly for every allowable digit tuple and checks exactly these constraints, so it enumerates the complete valid set and thus produces the exact sum. In contest solving, one can leverage structure: for two digits in base 10, the jth constraint becomes b ≡ 0 (mod d_j) on the other term, yielding the classical reduction a | b and b | 10a ⇒ b | 10; for higher bases and lengths, similar modular reductions identify restricted digit patterns and residue classes of N modulo the lcm of the constraints. Our instances require navigating multiple interacting moduli, ensuring the problem is nontrivial and not solvable by mere guessing.
source_question: Find the sum of all positive two-digit integers that are divisible by each of their digits.
